acceptance: HTTPS remains the default. Native BOSL execution is selected only when authenticated HTTPS is unavailable and the exact required tool and schema are freshly advertised for the selected authorized context; stale, missing or merely similar descriptors fail closed.

Registration sends the unchanged locally validated BOSL document as document, graph export sends an empty object, and returned actions preserve the exact href. Action payloads satisfy the returned schema and are omitted for bodyless actions. Business arguments reject context handles, credentials and authority selectors.

Native results are accepted only after exact selected-context verification. HTTP status, body or error and Retry-After are preserved for existing registration and lifecycle validation; malformed envelopes, mismatched contexts and refusals cannot become success.

Registration does not implicitly start execution. Explicit returned Start, effect approvals, server-owned progression, uncertain-outcome recovery and terminal behavior remain intact. Throttling preserves the existing explicit-request requirement for a later registration attempt.

Canonical guidance and every applicable generated package include the helper and equivalent scoped execution instructions while preserving existing operational compatibility, credential containment and product ownership boundaries.

CRM detail delivery retains graph completion after clarification, all intermediate nodes and edges on the selected route, compact app-ranked or shortest structural presentation, precise partial graphs, ranking provenance and explicit format overrides. Labels remain plain text, native inline visualization takes priority, unsupported Mermaid and ASCII do not complete delivery, and the focused student-workflow exception remains intact.

A renamed synthetic checkout fails admission before repair and admits a fresh controller after explicit append-only retirement. The first new admission links to the retired head, completes normally and leaves every pre-existing record byte-identical.

Relocation records form a canonical numbered hash chain with contiguous roots, cumulative per-chain retirement boundaries and the current real Git directory identity. Existing source paths, identical or unknown roots, unsupported Git directory types, malformed chains, tampering, empty retirement and copied post-relocation directories fail closed. Repeated renames preserve cumulative retirement correctly.

Each admission chain is classified independently. Old-root segments may retire; empty and wholly current-root segments remain unchanged with their existing checks. Mixed or foreign-root segments reject, and records beyond a retired boundary cannot evade current identity validation.

Retirement refuses live controllers and registered reviewer groups, including orphan descendants. Only validated old-to-current controller-directory mapping is used for liveness inspection; malformed, unreadable or indeterminate liveness evidence refuses retirement.

Retired admissions never provide live ownership, terminal results, children, checkpoint eligibility or historical approval. A pre-relocation copy receives only fresh admission capability and requires new reviews and receipts. Existing current-chain owner and checkpoint protections remain effective.

Relocation uses an exclusively held, safely admitted metadata lock and immutable publication, rechecks all chain heads before publication and fails closed on concurrent movement. Interrupted or competing operations cannot rewrite records, expose retired results or admit an unchecked owner.

Generated-output proof exports the exact candidate, removes only the declared generated namespace and runs the candidate's package generator with a bounded timeout. Complete regenerated and candidate inventories match in path, type, mode and blob identity; unexpected, missing, changed or unsupported entries, generator failure, timeout and canonical-file edits produce no deterministic coverage.

Source skill metadata receives deterministic coverage only for an existing publication-baseline skill with unchanged name, file type, mode and every byte outside the permitted version and requirement values, a strictly increased valid version, an identical dependency-name set and exact current candidate dependency pins. All ambiguous metadata and every other change remain assigned to independent source review.

Native deterministic coverage binds the exact candidate and publication baseline, generator command, all consumed source and history inputs, dependency and runtime identities, environment, exit status, regenerated inventory and verified paths. Missing, altered, stale, foreign or model-supplied proof cannot exclude paths or satisfy completeness; generation leaves canonical source, Git candidate and existing approval records unchanged.

Partitioning, complete-assessment admission and retained pending-path accounting consistently recognize only valid native deterministic coverage. Every other required canonical path remains independently reviewed, unresolved findings retain their existing resolution requirements, and changed inputs invalidate affected proof without carrying approval or rewriting historical outcomes.

Interrupted cohorts retain an ordered, typed checkpoint journal under existing managed metadata custody. Every admitted observation binds its plan, packet and actual consumed input identities; clean coverage includes its assigned primary path, and findings retain the complete actionable schema and stable identity. Foreign assignments, unknown inputs, stale digests, invalid prefixes and conflicting duplicates grant no coverage. Replay stops at malformed or truncated records while preserving the preceding valid observations and original execution outcome.

Journal reconciliation retains established findings as open ledger entries and prevents later findings or withdrawals from leaving earlier affected clean coverage eligible. Interrupted work remains ERROR or INCOMPLETE and cannot issue approval. Real controller-to-aggregate-to-series tests demonstrate retained observations, immutable original artifacts, unfinished-path reassignment and unchanged receipt gates.

Integration reuse admits only REVIEWED or justified NOT_APPLICABLE observations with matching consumed inputs, candidate tree, publication-range digest, required-path identity digest, open-finding ledger digest and observation guards. Candidate additions, deletions, mode or type changes, baseline movement, relevant finding changes and guard changes reassign concerns. UNREVIEWED observations never satisfy completion; all six concerns and a fresh complete-range classification remain mandatory.

Every cohort receives complete authoritative document bytes with exact path and digest provenance in its sealed governance input. The actual reviewer prompt preserves precedence and instructs consumption of those supplied texts without redundant fetching. Missing, altered, truncated or oversized mandatory governance fails closed rather than substituting summaries; any authority change changes the bundle and packet bindings.

Non-crosscutting assignments contain at most six primary paths per cohort with distinct cohort identities and noncolliding new-finding prefixes. Splitting preserves every required assignment exactly once, specialist authority restrictions and the crosscutting classification role. Execution retains at most three concurrent reviewers, the existing reviewer deadline, original request clocks and complete-candidate approval requirements.

Release preparation, prepared-record validation, deterministic publication and published-state verification consistently use release/<major>.<minor>.<patch>. Legacy IDE-specific release refs and malformed release refs are rejected for new operations. Publication safety admits release/* push events and resolves their gate base from origin/main while preserving existing main, source-ref and tag handling, exact-source CI, leased promotion and remote readback. Existing remote legacy refs remain untouched.

An exact-context native envelope marked isError:true cannot expose a successful registration, lifecycle action or graph result, even with a success-shaped body and successful HTTP status. Preserve a valid returned public error when present; otherwise refuse the envelope. Valid isError:false responses and existing refusal handling remain compatible.

Journal observations become eligible only for interrupted cohorts with intact original per-cohort preparation seals and intact shared plan and context. Altered source pages, schema, governance, context, seals or shared preparation admit neither clean coverage nor integration observations. Retain original raw journal bytes and unfinished or error outcomes without approval.

Journal coverage names only real assigned paths present in the sealed input inventory, and every consumed input binds a real current identity with its exact digest. Virtual retained-criterion paths and input identities never enter replayed source coverage; native criterion expansion remains responsible for those obligations.

The sealed cohort packet digest includes its final governance-bundle and checkpoint-journal bindings. An intact interrupted cohort can recover its eligible observations through the actual recovery consumer; changing either binding rejects adoption while preserving original artifacts and execution status.

Synthetic review workspaces supply every mandatory governing document and imported executable dependency, including the generated-output proof module, and reviewer stubs accept and forward the governance stdin payload. The immutable fourteen-module review-policy inventory remains unchanged. Review-series, governance, performance, source-frontier and publication-admission runners discover and execute their complete declared cases without skips, weakened assertions or substituted production behavior; publication admission declares all 36 cases.

Cross-area publication and review-evidence custody require adversarial focused cases and actual completeness, pending-path, controller, lifecycle and publication interactions.
